description: MeshCom Web Push wire contract. Shared by mc-chat and MCProxy via the `contract/` git subtree (mc-chat is upstream); each repo's test suite implements these vectors. Frontend mirrors match_vectors + eligibility for its foreground-sound predicate. Edit in mc-chat and re-sync — never edit MCProxy's copy in place. v2 (2026-07-17) adds via-routed dst resolution, push eligibility, dedup, and payload_vectors after a cross-backend parity audit found the two backends diverging on all four. v3 (2026-07-17) adds a blocklist push-path gate: a message whose resolved source is on the node's GLOBAL blocked_callsigns set produces zero pushes (checked together with eligibility, BEFORE dedup/matching) — closing a bug where the push dispatcher bypassed the blocklist every other path enforces. v4 (2026-07-26) moves to the subtree (this file previously lived outside it at mc-chat's tests/fixtures/, kept byte-identical by hand) and adds eligibility clause (c): text ACKs and {CET} time broadcasts are not push-eligible, closing a bug where every message the operator sent produced an ':ackNNN' notification.

subscribe.semantics: Upsert by subscription.endpoint. Re-POSTing the same endpoint with a new filter overwrites the stored filter (this is how a pref change persists — there is no separate prefs endpoint). A malformed or missing filter field is coerced to filter_defaults; groups:null must be treated as [] and never crash the matcher.

unsubscribe.semantics: Delete the row whose endpoint matches. Idempotent: unsubscribing a missing endpoint still returns ok:true.

dst_resolution: A via-routed destination is 'VIA[,VIA2],TARGET' — the real target is the LAST comma-separated component, trimmed (mirrors each backend's compute_conversation_key / _resolve_target: e.g. 'OE1KBC-12,232' -> '232', 'OE1KBC-12,DK5EN-99' -> 'DK5EN-99'). A dst with no comma is its own target. On a LoRa mesh, relay-hopped frames are the COMMON case, so this resolution is required, not an edge case. Both backends AND the frontend foreground-sound predicate MUST resolve dst identically before matching.
src_resolution: A src carries the relay path the OTHER way round — the FIRST comma-separated component is the real sender (e.g. 'DK5EN-99,OE1KBC-12' -> 'DK5EN-99'). SSID is kept.
eligibility: Checked ONCE per message, BEFORE per-subscription matching. A message is push-eligible IFF: (a) it is a chat text message — exclude telemetry (type:'tele'), position beacons (type:'pos'), and any non-text/no-text frame; AND (b) its resolved source (first comma-component of src) is NOT equal to the node's own callsign — never push the user's own outbound sends or mesh-echoes of them; AND (c) it is not a text ACK and not a {CET} time broadcast. An ineligible message produces zero pushes and does not open or feed a coalesce window.
eligibility_noise_semantics: Clause (c) detail, evaluated on the SAME text extraction as clause (a) (msg-or-text fallback). A frame is noise iff that text CONTAINS the substring ':ack' OR STARTS WITH '{CET}'. Both are type:'msg' frames, so clause (a) cannot catch them. Text ACK: the mesh answers every outbound message with a '<CALL>  :ackNNN' frame addressed back to the sender, so with the default filter.dm=true the operator got one notification per message they sent. The substring test is deliberately as BROAD as the exclusion MCProxy's message queries already apply (`msg NOT LIKE '%:ack%'`): a push must never announce a message that no conversation view will show, and matching the query exactly is what keeps the two consistent. The known cost is that a chat message legitimately containing ':ack' is silent — accepted, because such a message is equally invisible in the message list. {CET}: a periodic network time broadcast; MCProxy's storage layer refuses to even persist these, yet every broadcast:true subscriber was notified for each one.
dedup: A logical message may reach the backend more than once (multiple gateways, UDP retransmits) — this is why storage dedups on a ~60-min window. Push must fire AT MOST ONCE per logical message. Dedup key: msg_id within the dedup window when msg_id is truthy, else the tuple (resolved-src, resolved-dst, text). A duplicate must neither produce a second immediate push NOR increment a coalesce summary count.
blocklist: Checked ONCE per message, together with eligibility and BEFORE dedup/matching. If the message's resolved source (src_resolution, case-insensitive) is an element of the node's blocked_callsigns set, produce ZERO pushes and do not open or feed any coalesce window. blocked_callsigns is the node's GLOBAL blocklist (admin kickban + curated sperrliste), NOT a per-subscription field. A message merely RELAYED THROUGH a blocked node (blocked callsign appears as a via-hop, not the first comma-component) is NOT suppressed.
match_semantics: Given an incoming eligible message with destination `dst`, the node's own configured callsign `own`, and a subscription's stored `filter`: first resolve `dst` per dst_resolution to `target`. Push to that subscription IFF ( target == own AND filter.dm ) OR ( target == '*' AND filter.broadcast ) OR ( target is an element of filter.groups, compared as trimmed strings ). A DM whose target is any other callsign never pushes.

match_vectors.name: group with surrounding whitespace still matches

eligibility_vectors.name: own outbound send is NOT eligible
own mesh-echo (via-routed src resolves to own) is NOT eligible
text ACK addressed back to us is NOT eligible (clause c)
text ACK read from the msg key is NOT eligible (clause c)
{CET} time broadcast is NOT eligible (clause c)
ordinary chat mentioning the word ack IS eligible - only ':ack' is noise
{CET} not at the start IS eligible - the marker is a prefix

blocklist_vectors.name: via-routed src resolves to real sender before block check
relay hop is NOT the sender - message via a blocked relay still pushes

payload_schema.src: sender callsign string, as received (raw, may carry the relay path)
payload_schema.dst: destination string as received (raw, may carry the relay path) — NOT resolved in the payload
payload_schema.text: chat text: str(msg.get('msg') or msg.get('text') or ''), truncated to <= 120 chars
payload_schema.ts: epoch SECONDS (number). If the source timestamp is epoch milliseconds it MUST be divided by 1000; a non-numeric value passes through unchanged.

payload_vectors.name: ms timestamp converts to epoch seconds; text from msg field
text falls back to the text key and truncates at 120 chars
null msg coerces to empty string, not the literal 'None'

coalesce.semantics: Per-subscription rate limit. On an eligible+matching+non-duplicate message: if no window is open for this subscription, push it immediately (single-message payload) and open a 5s window. Messages that match while a window is open are buffered (not pushed). When the window closes, if the buffer is non-empty, emit exactly ONE summary push { count: len(buffer), latest: <payload of the last buffered message> } and close the window. The next matching message after the window is closed opens a fresh window with an immediate push. Uses an injectable now() clock in tests — never real wall-clock. Recommend a monotonic clock in production so an NTP step cannot stretch or collapse the window.

scenarios.name: two matching messages within the 5s window -> immediate + one summary
single message -> one immediate push, no summary
a duplicate (same msg_id) within the window neither re-pushes nor increments the summary count

prune_semantics: When pywebpush delivery to a subscription returns any of these HTTP status codes, delete that subscription row. 401/403 catch stale-VAPID subscriptions after a key regeneration; 404/410 catch expired endpoints. Keep the subscription on any other status (e.g. 500) or a transient connection error. Pruning only on 404/410 would leave a dead-VAPID subscription failing forever.
execution_isolation: The mesh-message ingest handler MUST NOT await push delivery. It only enqueues to an in-process queue; a background task drains the queue and calls pywebpush via asyncio.to_thread with explicit connect (~3s) and read (~5s) timeouts. The SSE broadcast of the message happens independently of, and never blocks on, push delivery. Delivery tasks/coroutines must be strongly referenced until done (never fire-and-forget an unreferenced create_task — it can be GC-dropped mid-flight).
vapid: Keypair generated once per install at first use, persisted OUTSIDE the repo (mc-chat: ~/.meshcom-mock/vapid.json; MCProxy: /var/lib/mcapp/vapid.json), never committed.
